name: rsi_extreme_reversion_5s_2
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: Extreme RSI readings (< 15 or > 85) on 1-min bars in liquid large-caps signal exhaustion of short-term momentum. Retail traders overshoot due to panic/greed, and institutional algorithms provide liquidity at extremes. The inefficiency persists because most RSI-based strategies use 14-period on daily charts — the 1-minute version with extreme thresholds catches micro-panics that aren't visible on higher timeframes. Speed of mean reversion on 1-min makes this hard to execute manually.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.

filters.volume_filter: rel_volume > 1.5 — need genuine participation not thin tape

weaknesses: RSI < 15 can persist for dozens of bars in genuine selloffs — the 'catching a falling knife' problem
High trade frequency means costs compound; need very tight slippage management
7-period RSI on 1-min is extremely noisy — false extremes in low-volume periods
prior_art: Connors RSI short-term mean reversion; adapted to 1-min Indian equities
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
